findings.topic: Typography — display serif candidates (verified facts)
findings.detail: INSTRUMENT SERIF: condensed display serif by Rodrigo Fuenzalida with Instrument (dir. Jordan Egstad, JD Hooge, Jack De Caluwé), SIL OFL 1.1, 'designed for large sizes'. Google Fonts serves ONLY weight 400 regular + italic (confirmed via fonts.googleapis.com css2 response) — any weight hierarchy must come from the sans. Directory listings tag it for 'webpage headers and luxury branding'; commonly paired with Instrument Sans, Inter, IBM Plex Mono; one pairing site calls it 'Cormorant Garamond but more contemporary'. FRAUNCES: variable 'Old Style soft-serif' (Windsor/Souvenir/Cooper lineage) by Undercase Type (Phaedra Charles, Flavia Zimbardi); axes opsz 9–144, wght 100–900, SOFT 0–100, WONK 0–1; WONK auto-substitutes above ~opsz 18 and the README says wonky forms are 'less desirable for continuous reading'; Google serves wght 100–900 + italics. Evidence conflicts on fit: one directory pins it to food/packaging, fontalternatives.com recommends it for 'fashion brands, style publications, luxury apparel' — treat as the WARMER option. CORMORANT GARAMOND: Christian Thalmann (Catharsis), OFL; Google serves 300/400/500/600/700 + italics; family includes Garamond, Infant, Unicase, Upright, SC variants; pairing writers warn its hairlines 'thin out at body sizes on screen' → display only (≥28px). PLAYFAIR DISPLAY: Google serves 400–900 + italics; the separate 'Playfair' v2.2 (Claus Eggers Sørensen, OFL) is a 3-axis variable (wdth, wght, opsz 'Agate→Needlepoint'); reads 'fashion magazine'/Didone. DM SERIF DISPLAY: 400 + italic only. Bodoni Moda is the Google Fonts Didone with an opsz axis (inferred from prior knowledge, not re-verified).

findings.topic: Typography — sans body/UI candidates
findings.detail: INTER: v4.x, OFL 1.1, wght 100–900 with an optical-size axis ('text' = taller x-height/ink traps; 'display' = cleaner for large sizes); Google Fonts accepts `Inter:opsz,wght@14..32,100..900`; rsms recommends `font-feature-settings:'liga' 1,'calt' 1` and InterVariable via @supports. Pairing writers: under a display serif Inter 'becomes close to invisible, which is the entire appeal'. MANROPE: Google serves 200–800 (variable); described as softer/more geometric than Inter; 'Cormorant Garamond + Manrope' called 'the most elegant' pairing on one 2026 list (GitHub README returned 404). GEIST: Vercel, OFL; on Google Fonts but Google's build 'lacks the full glyph set and font-feature-settings support' — npm `geist` package recommended; search evidence positions it for dev tools/SaaS, i.e. weakest luxury evidence of the three. SATOSHI: NOT on Google Fonts; Fontshare/ITF Free Font License — secondary sources say free commercial web use is granted but redistribution/self-hosting copies is restricted and serving via Fontshare's CSS API is the contemplated route; one listing says 'free for personal use' — CONFLICT, read License/FFL.txt in the official download before using. Fontshare's own pages did not render for the fetcher (reachable=false).

findings.topic: Typography — pairings seen in the wild / templates
findings.detail: Swiper Studio's 'Hero – Split Screen' template (a fashion-magazine-style hero) uses Instrument Serif for display + Inter for UI on an off-white background with a single green accent. Third-party extraction of jacquemus.com (captured during a maintenance window; live site returned 403 to the fetcher) shows ONE geometric sans (Futura PTT) at 18px / 400 / 0.56px letter-spacing, pure #ffffff/#000000, border-radius 0 everywhere, a single 1px black hairline as the only divider, 50px section padding, 20px side margins, 32px paragraph spacing. Third-party brand analysis of The Row: 'restrained, high-contrast serif wordmark … black on cream', no official typeface documented. Toteme: a bespoke 'Toteme Sans' (Ateljé Altmann, 2023) exists — link to the site is inferred from the name only. findings.topic: 2025–2026 editorial-luxury direction (trend commentary, agency sources)
findings.detail: Recurring claims: quiet-luxury houses (Bottega Veneta, Aesop) favour 'editorial discipline, long-form product storytelling, near-zero visual noise'; 2026 typography trend pieces push 'maximalist'/high-contrast serifs for hero headings while 'refined serif fonts for headings signal editorial polish, luxury'; variable fonts + subtle animation; kinetic type reacting to scroll/cursor used sparingly to guide the eye; Figma's trend guide: 'tune easing … smooth for luxury, snappy for playful brands'; dark UI positioned as 'a premium signal for beauty, fashion, jewelry'; a counter-view warns that 'empty white space and a single centered paragraph' now reads as unfinished — the fix is brand character through typography, spacing and motion. One agency reports small purposeful transitions (cart drawer sliding in with the just-added product visible) moved sales on apparel tests (figures not published).

findings.topic: Colour system — ivory/bone/charcoal + one accent
findings.detail: Reference hexes from palette guides: Ivory #FFFFF0, Navy #1B2A4A, Charcoal #36454F ('Classic elegant: Ivory · Navy · Gold #D4AF37 · Charcoal'); alternate luxury set Deep Navy #14213D, Charcoal #1C1C1C, Cream #F5F0E1. Palette structure rule (Zoviz 2026 guide): cap at 3–4 colours — one deep anchor (black/navy/oxblood/green), one metallic accent, 1–2 quiet neutrals (ivory/cream/taupe). 'Bone' had no sourced hex (≈#E3DAC9 from memory, unverified). Awwwards fashion/luxury e-commerce winners list near-monochrome palettes: Tilly Sveaas #ffffff/#080808; The Tie-break #FFFFFF; Serotoninn #ED3833/#000000; Coutumes #F9AF26/#000000 — i.e. neutral base + at most one accent. COMPUTED LOCALLY (WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula, py -3.12): charcoal #1C1C1A on ivory #F6F3EE = 15.42:1; navy #1B2A4A on ivory = 12.85:1; navy on bone #EAE5DC = 11.34:1; ivory on navy = 12.85:1 (all AAA); muted grey #6B6761 on ivory = 5.08:1 (AA pass) but on bone = 4.48:1 (FAILS AA for normal text) → muted captions need ≥#5E5A54-ish on bone or stay on ivory. Pale grey on ivory is the classic luxury contrast failure.

findings.topic: Hero — full-bleed video: browser policies
findings.detail: iOS/WebKit (policy since iOS 10): `<video autoplay muted>` or a source with NO audio track autoplays without a gesture; `playsinline` required on iPhone or it goes fullscreen; autoplaying video starts only when on screen and pauses when scrolled out; unmuting without a gesture pauses it; `play()` returns a Promise rejected when blocked. iOS LOW POWER MODE blocks autoplay and rejects play() with NotAllowedError (WebKit bug 216887; WebKit's response: 'sounds like desirable behavior'); WebKit deliberately overlays a native play button in Low Power Mode that lives in a closed shadow root and cannot be hidden (bug 219889 'Won't Fix'); no API exposes Low Power Mode. One informal source says Safari sometimes throws synchronously rather than rejecting → wrap play() in try/catch AND .catch. Chrome: muted autoplay is always allowed; always check the play() promise and never show a pause state before playback starts. `navigator.connection.saveData === true` signals the user's reduced-data preference (Chromium-only API; Firefox/Safari lack it) with the `Save-Data` request header as the server-side counterpart.

findings.topic: Hero — full-bleed video: Core Web Vitals & loading
findings.detail: web.dev: set width/height on <video> so the browser reserves space (no CLS); when a video is the LCP element, LCP = time the POSTER renders, and 'videos without a poster attribute are currently not considered for LCP' → always ship a poster; preload the poster with `<link rel=preload as=image fetchpriority=high>` (fetchpriority can't be set on the poster attribute itself); never `loading=lazy` on the LCP video; `loading=lazy` on below-fold videos defers the poster too; browsers default to preload=metadata which 'can download more data than expected' → use preload=none for non-autoplay video; GIF-replacement recipe = autoplay muted loop playsinline + IntersectionObserver fallback that only sets autoplay when in view. Baymard homepage research: keep ad-like content out of the hero (55% fail), don't autorotate carousels on mobile, 5–7s per header-only slide on desktop, pause on hover, 'static homepage sections often perform better'.

findings.topic: Hero — video encoding budgets for mobile
findings.detail: Viget: target 700–1,200 kb/s, 1280x720 via ffmpeg size preset, strip audio with `-an`; other guides: 10–15 s loop (15–30 s if repetition is noticeable), start ~1500 kbps and lower until artifacts, 24 fps, resolution matched to rendered size (serve 480p/720p/1080p variants), H.264 baseline + VP9/AV1/HEVC where supported; Mux: a 10-s hero loop as a low-quality HLS mobile rendition ≈ 400–800 KB vs 8–15 MB for a self-hosted 1080p MP4 (illustrative, not benchmarked); Mux's stance: 'decorative hero video doesn't need pristine quality on every connection; it needs to play without buffering'. Community budgets: '<10 s, <2 MB, no audio track'. Webflow-world guidance: hide the background video below the tablet breakpoint and let the poster take over; Elfsight: respect prefers-reduced-motion and consider poster-only on mobile. A separate 9:16 crop for phones is my inference (not sourced).

findings.topic: Hero — split hero and slow Ken Burns stills
findings.detail: Split hero: an even 50/50 'reads as symmetric and loses the editorial quality' — pattern library recommends 60/40 or 70/30 with the LARGER column for imagery; a Converge fashion template uses ~55/45 with an oversized italic serif headline on a muted olive block; Swiper's split template stacks below 768px and re-sets at 1024/1280 — whichever half is second lands below the fold on phones, so order deliberately. Ken Burns: animate a pseudo-element/img inside an overflow:hidden box, `scale(1.05)→scale(1.1)` over ~20s with `forwards`; Slider Revolution recommends LINEAR easing for pan/zoom (ease-out front-loads motion); scale the image layer, not the container (scaling the container breaks background-size:cover); disable under prefers-reduced-motion; Divi/Slider Revolution use 1.5–2x which is too much for luxury (inferred).

findings.topic: Motion — Lenis smooth scroll (v1.3.x, measured defaults)
findings.detail: Defaults from README: lerp 0.1; duration 1.2 s (ignored when lerp is set); easing `(t) => Math.min(1, 1.001 - Math.pow(2, -10 * t))`; smoothWheel true; syncTouch false ('can be unstable on iOS<16'); syncTouchLerp 0.075; touchInertiaExponent 1.7; autoRaf false; autoResize true; anchors false (anchor links don't work unless `anchors:true`); allowNestedScroll false (costly — use `data-lenis-prevent` instead). GSAP wiring: `lenis.on('scroll', ScrollTrigger.update); gsap.ticker.add(t => lenis.raf(t*1000)); gsap.ticker.lagSmoothing(0)`. React: `import { ReactLenis, useLenis } from 'lenis/react'`; `<ReactLenis root options={{ autoRaf:false }} ref={lenisRef}/>` then drive `lenisRef.current.lenis.raf(time*1000)` from gsap.ticker; a Framer Motion `frame.update` integration is also documented. Drawers/modals/nested scroll: add `data-lenis-prevent` (or -wheel/-touch variants); `lenis.stop()/start()` to lock page scroll while a drawer is open. Limitations: no CSS scroll-snap (use lenis/snap), Safari capped at 60 fps and 30 fps in Low Power Mode, position:fixed may lag on pre-M1 Safari, iframes break wheel forwarding. Import `lenis/dist/lenis.css`. Lower lerp = heavier glide (0.07–0.08 is a common 'luxury' setting — inferred, not sourced).

findings.topic: Motion — GSAP 3.13+ (free), ScrollTrigger, SplitText, React hook
findings.detail: Since GSAP 3.13 (29 Apr 2025, after Webflow acquisition) the whole toolset incl. SplitText, MorphSVG, ScrollSmoother etc. is free 'even for commercial use' and ships in the main npm package. ScrollTrigger: `trigger/start/end` ('top 80%'), `scrub:true` (direct) or `scrub:1` (1-second catch-up smoothing), `pin`, `toggleActions:'play none none reverse'`, `once:true`, `markers` for dev; start defaults 'top bottom', end 'bottom top'; `gsap.matchMedia()` is the responsive/reduced-motion mechanism (`mm.add('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) and (min-width: 800px)', …)` — reduced-motion usage is general practice, not on the page); `ScrollTrigger.batch('.card', { start:'top 85%', onEnter: b => gsap.to(b,{opacity:1,y:0,stagger:0.15}) })` for grids; `scrollerProxy` exists for proxies but Lenis uses the ticker approach above. Default ease is `power1.out`; eases available: power1–4, expo, circ, sine, back, elastic, bounce, none, steps (+ rough/slow/expoScale, CustomEase). SplitText rewrite: `SplitText.create(el, { type:'lines', mask:'lines', autoSplit:true, aria:'auto', onSplit(self){ return gsap.from(self.lines, { yPercent:100, opacity:0, duration:0.6, stagger:0.1, ease:'expo.out' }) } })` — autoSplit re-splits on font load/resize and onSplit returning a tween carries progress over; 50% smaller, adds aria-label/aria-hidden; split after `document.fonts.ready`. React: `@gsap/react` `useGSAP(() => {...}, { scope: containerRef })` auto-reverts tweens/ScrollTriggers/SplitText on unmount (handles React 18 StrictMode double-effects); wrap event-driven tweens in `contextSafe`.

findings.topic: Motion — Motion (ex-Framer Motion) API values
findings.detail: Framer Motion became independent 'Motion' on 12 Nov 2024; upgrade guide: uninstall framer-motion, `npm i motion`, import from `'motion/react'` (`'motion/react-client'` for RSC); v12 has no breaking changes for React; the IntersectionObserver fallback for whileInView was removed in v10. `whileInView` + `viewport={{ once:true, amount:'some'|'all'|0–1 (default 'some'), margin:'0px', root }}`. Tween defaults: duration 0.3 s (0.8 s with keyframes), named eases linear/easeIn/easeOut/easeInOut/circ*/back*/anticipate or cubic-bezier arrays. Springs: `bounce` default 0.25 (0 = critically damped), `visualDuration` overrides duration; physics mode stiffness/damping/mass (setting these ignores bounce/duration). Orchestration: `delayChildren: stagger(0.1, { from:'first'|'last'|'center' })` (docs document this instead of staggerChildren). Scroll: `useScroll({ target: ref, offset:['start end','end start'] })` → `useTransform(scrollYProgress,[0,1],['-10%','10%'])` for parallax; smooth with `useSpring(v,{ stiffness:100, damping:30, restDelta:0.001 })`; `layoutId` enables shared-element transitions (card → quick-view). Community consensus reveal recipe: ease `[0.16, 1, 0.3, 1]` (expo-out), y 24–40 px, duration 0.6–1.0 s, `viewport={{ once:true, amount:0.2 }}` or margin -80/-100px, stagger 0.08–0.12 s.

findings.topic: Motion — image clip-path reveals, parallax, marquee, magnetic buttons, CSS scroll-driven
findings.detail: CLIP-PATH REVEAL (GSAP forum consensus): use `gsap.fromTo(img, { clipPath:'inset(0% 100% 0% 0%)' }, { clipPath:'inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)', ease:'none', scrollTrigger:{ trigger, start:'top 80%', end:'bottom 40%', scrub:true } })`; put units on EVERY value including zeros, declare both ends with fromTo (browsers return ambiguous shorthand), no CSS transition on the tweened property, polygon() is the fallback if inset() jumps; put the clip-path on the media only. PARALLAX: image at 120% height / top:-10% inside overflow:hidden, tween `yPercent` −8→+8 with `ease:'none'` and scrub — keep travel 5–15% (sketch from general practice; no 2025 source found). MARQUEE (Ryan Mulligan): duplicate the list with `aria-hidden=true`, flex + `min-width:100%` + `flex-shrink:0`, keyframe `to { transform: translateX(calc(-100% - var(--gap))) }` (plain −100% misaligns), decorative only, no focusable children, slow speeds (dash.fi pattern: 60 s linear, hairline rules, edge mask-fade, stops fully under reduced motion; Quackit: `flex-wrap:wrap` fallback), pause on hover/focus-within optional, never `<marquee>`. MAGNETIC BUTTON: `gsap.quickTo(el,'x',{ duration:1, ease:'elastic.out(1,0.3)' })` (Craft UI; Osmo uses the same quickTo + xPercent/yPercent −50 cursor pattern), offset = cursor − element centre × 0.3–0.5 strength ('beyond 0.5 feels like running away'), reset to 0 on mouseleave; pointer devices only (inferred: gate with `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`). CSS SCROLL-DRIVEN (`animation-timeline: view()`): Chrome/Edge 115+ (2023), Safari 26 (Sep 2025), Firefox still behind a flag in stable as of mid-2026, ~82.6% global → progressive enhancement only, finished state as default inside `@supports (animation-timeline: view())` and `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.

findings.topic: Product card hover behaviours & listing UX
findings.detail: Standard fashion pattern: second photo fades in on hover (desktop); on mobile a tap swaps and reverts after ~2 s (Fudge); key the swap to image slot #2; preload the alt image on hover-intent or when the card enters view to avoid flash; limit the hover trigger to the image area so it doesn't override a swatch-selected image (Shopify thread). Quick-add on the same hover (Grana: button on lower half of image → sizes appear on hover); Visually reports a size-selector-on-hover test at +4.2% revenue (single vendor); Growthsuite's 25–40%/10–15% figures are unsourced → discount; quick-add 'can backfire for high-consideration products'. Baymard: show sizes as BUTTONS not dropdowns (users found their size out of stock only after opening a dropdown); 44 px touch targets; announce price/availability changes with aria-live. Luxury restraint examples: Ben Sherman 'only a glimpse of a category image on rollover', Missguided's add-to-bag turning transparent, All Saints flipping every product to the same angle, Reebok swatch hover recolouring the main image, ASOS quick view/save on hover, Boohoo's zoom judged 'distracting'. Toteme's PLP grid/lifestyle toggle + in-grid video blocks is the editorial-luxury listing precedent. Hover zoom values (scale 1.03–1.05 over 600–900 ms, ease-out) are convention, not sourced. Pakistani unstitched conventions: Sapphire's unstitched listings expose only a PRICE filter, handle fabric (lawn/dobby/jacquard) in copy, split by piece count (2-pc/3-pc), put colour in the product name ('Blue Floral 3Pc'); Biba (India) shows colour/fabric facets with counts — the better model; because unstitched is buyer-tailored, SIZE is a weak filter vs fabric, colour, pieces, embroidery, price (inferred).

findings.topic: Navigation — mega menu (desktop) vs drawer (mobile)
findings.detail: Baymard: hover mega menus are the primary nav at 88% of top US e-commerce sites; hover-intent delay of 300–500 ms eliminates most accidental triggering (61% of sites don't — 'flickering/flimsy'), consider a mouse-path/diagonal algorithm; chunk lists when they reach ~10 categories (users overwhelmed beyond ~10); make drop-down headers clickable to the parent category (33% don't); highlight the current scope (95% don't); 'mobile navigation is particularly difficult' — the mobile menu 'will often have to deviate significantly from the desktop mega drop-down'; hamburger is the default; make PRODUCT CATEGORIES the top-level items (33% nest them under 'Shop'); style secondary links (account, stores, help) smaller, below a separator; show popular categories + 'More' for big catalogs; use full-scope link text on mobile ('Women's New Arrivals', 59% don't); each visual element one hit area. NN/g: open after ~0.5 s hover, render within 0.1 s, keep open 0.5 s after the pointer leaves, tolerate the diagonal path; most important group top-left; show each choice once; no search box inside the menu; hiding nav behind a hamburger cut discoverability by >20% in a 179-person study — 'combo' (some links visible + hamburger) was used 86% vs 57% for hidden-only on phones; repeating nav at the page bottom helps. Vendor consensus: 3–5 visible header links + hamburger, drill-down tiers (not a shrunken desktop panel), 44–48 px tap targets, start collapsed. CART DRAWER: drawer by default with a 'View full bag' escape hatch; auto-open after add-to-bag (otherwise 'just a prettier cart page'); show the added item with variant, line items with qty/remove, subtotal, one small upsell at most; evidence is mixed (one test: desktop +17%, mobile −8.4%; multi-item sessions find drawers annoying) — all vendor-sourced, none from Baymard.

findings.topic: Mobile-first bottom bars & sticky CTA
findings.detail: NN/g: bottom tab bars are the iOS norm, stay visible while scrolling, suit a SMALL number of destinations (3–5 per app guides); once tabs overflow into a carousel the hidden ones lose discoverability; NN/g on iOS 26: cramped tab bars with a permanent search button shrink tap targets. Hoober's observational study (≈1,300 sightings): 49% of people interacting held the phone one-handed, thumbs did ~75% of interactions, only ~one-third of the screen (bottom, opposite the thumb) is effortless; later revised to 'fewer than 50% one-handed'. University of Waikato thesis: users preferred a bottom bar over a top-left hamburger on m-commerce layouts (sample size not shown — directional). Sticky add-to-cart: appear once the original CTA scrolls out of view (not on load; one vendor says after 50% scroll — disagree, test), carry price + variant, stay thin; ~50% of audited stores keep ATC within reach; touch targets 44–48 px with ~32 px spacing; vendor lift claims (8.7% ATC, '10–25%', '7.9% Baymard') are unverified and one test lost conversion/revenue; Baymard's own sticky-ATC guidance is paywalled. Lenis note: position:fixed bars can lag on pre-M1 Safari.

findings.topic: Research limitations / reachability
findings.detail: reachable=false: jacquemus.com (403), cos.com (403), fonts.google.com specimen pages (JS-rendered, title only — axis/weight data taken from the css2 API response and GitHub READMEs instead), fontshare.com (JS-rendered), godly.website (301 → recent.design, no fashion filter), sharanda/manrope README (404), Mux background-video article (guessed URL 404; a different Mux article was found via search), Baymard premium pages (paywalled). All conversion-lift percentages in this report come from vendors unless attributed to Baymard/NN/g; treat them as directional.

recommendations: TYPE STACK: Display = Instrument Serif (400 + italic; use italic for emphasis words in headlines, e.g. 'Lawn, *unstitched*'), UI/body = Manrope 200–800 (or Inter with opsz for a cooler voice). Load via Google Fonts css2 with explicit axes: `family=Instrument+Serif:ital@0;1&family=Manrope:wght@200..800&display=swap`, preconnect to fonts.gstatic.com, or self-host woff2 (Instrument Serif is OFL). Keep Fraunces (opsz 144, SOFT ~30–50, WONK 0) as the warmer alternate if the owner finds Instrument Serif too cool; avoid Cormorant below 28px and skip Satoshi unless the ITF FFL is read and served from Fontshare.

TYPE SCALE (mobile→desktop, clamp()): hero display 44→112px, Instrument Serif, line-height 0.95–1.0, letter-spacing −0.01em; section titles 32→56px; eyebrow/labels Manrope 11–12px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.12–0.16em, weight 500; body Manrope 15–17px/1.6; price Manrope 500 with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`. Since Instrument Serif has one weight, build hierarchy with size, italic and colour only.

COLOUR TOKENS (all pairs below verified ≥AA locally): --ivory #F6F3EE (page), --bone #EAE5DC (cards/alt sections), --charcoal #1C1C1A (ink, 15.4:1 on ivory), --navy #1B2A4A (accent: CTAs, links, active states; 12.9:1 on ivory), --ink-muted #5E5A54 (captions — #6B6761 fails AA on bone), --hairline rgba(28,28,26,.12), optional --dark #121212 for one cinematic lookbook section. Rule from the palette guides: one deep anchor + one accent + two neutrals, nothing else; WhatsApp green only on the WhatsApp CTA icon.

HERO (full-bleed fabric video): `<video autoplay muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="hero-poster.avif" width=1920 height=1080 aria-hidden="true">` with webm (VP9/AV1) + H.264 MP4 sources; 10–15 s loop, no audio track (`-an`), 720p, 700–1200 kb/s, 24 fps, target ≤2 MB; `<link rel=preload as=image href=hero-poster.avif fetchpriority=high>`; set `v.muted=true` in JS, `v.play().catch(()=>{})` inside try/catch and leave the poster when it fails (iOS Low Power Mode throws NotAllowedError and overlays a native play button you cannot hide); skip the video entirely when `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` or `navigator.connection?.saveData` is true; on viewports <768px either serve a separate 9:16 crop or show the poster only (Webflow-style breakpoint hide); overlay a 20–35% charcoal gradient for text legibility; no autorotating carousel on mobile.

ALT HEROES: lookbook/collection pages use an editorial split (60/40 image-dominant, text column with eyebrow + Instrument Serif headline + underlined text link, stacking image-first on mobile); category heroes use a slow Ken Burns still: `transform: scale(1.04)→scale(1.10)` over 18–24 s, linear, `forwards`, on an inside overflow:hidden, disabled under reduced motion.

MOTION ENGINE: one scroll clock — Lenis 1.3.x (`lerp 0.08`, `smoothWheel true`, `syncTouch false`, `autoRaf false`) driven from `gsap.ticker` with `lagSmoothing(0)`; GSAP 3.13+ (free) ScrollTrigger for scroll-linked work (`scrub: 1` for parallax, `toggleActions` for reveals, `ScrollTrigger.batch` for product grids with `start:'top 85%'`, `stagger 0.08–0.12`); Motion (`motion/react`) only for component state (drawer open/close spring `{ type:'spring', visualDuration:0.45, bounce:0.1 }`, quick-view `layoutId`, hover/tap). Wrap all GSAP in `useGSAP({ scope })`; add `data-lenis-prevent` to the bag drawer, quick-view and filter panels and call `lenis.stop()` while they are open.

MOTION VALUES (luxury = slow, no bounce): page/section reveals `y 32px → 0, opacity 0→1, 0.9–1.1 s, expo.out` (GSAP) or `[0.16,1,0.3,1]` (Motion), `once: true`, `amount 0.2`; headline line reveal via SplitText `mask:'lines', yPercent 100, 1.0–1.2 s, stagger 0.1, expo.out`, split after `document.fonts.ready` with `autoSplit:true`; image clip-path reveals `inset(0% 100% 0% 0%) → inset(0% 0% 0% 0%)` over 1.2 s expo.out (or scrubbed `top 80%`→`bottom 40%`), always `fromTo` with units on zeros; parallax ±8 yPercent on 120%-tall images, `ease:'none'`; hover zoom on cards `scale 1.04, 800 ms, cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)`; marquee (fabric names / 'Lawn · Cotton · Karandi') 50–60 s linear, duplicated set aria-hidden, mask-fade edges, static wrap under reduced motion; magnetic buttons desktop-only `(hover:hover) and (pointer:fine)`, quickTo 0.8–1 s `elastic.out(1,0.3)`, strength 0.35. Wrap everything in `gsap.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)')` and drop scrub/parallax under 768px.

PRODUCT CARDS: 4:5 image, second image (fabric close-up/drape) cross-fades on hover (desktop) and on tap-with-2s-revert (mobile), hover trigger limited to the image; preload image #2 when the card enters view; colour swatches under the price that switch the card image without being overridden by the hover; quick view (not quick add — unstitched is high-consideration) on hover/long-press opening a Motion `layoutId` sheet; 'Add to bag' inside quick view as a button, piece-count/fabric chips as buttons (Baymard: buttons not dropdowns), 44px targets, aria-live for price/stock; grid toggle 'Packshot / Styled' like Toteme and one video tile per 8–12 products.

FILTERS: facets = Fabric (lawn, cotton, embroidered, wash & wear, karandi), Colour (swatch chips), Pieces (2/3-pc, men's 4–5 m lengths), Price range, Collection; show counts per facet (Biba model, not Sapphire's price-only); on mobile a bottom-sheet filter panel with sticky 'Show N results'; no size facet (unstitched).

NAVIGATION: desktop header = Women / Men / Collections / Lookbook / Store with a hover mega menu that opens after 300–500 ms intent (Baymard) and closes 0.5 s after exit (NN/g), category headers clickable, ≤10 items per column, one editorial image per panel, current scope highlighted; mobile = hamburger drawer whose FIRST items are product categories (Women's Lawn, Women's Embroidered, Men's Wash & Wear…) with full-scope labels, secondary links (Store, Fabric care, Size guide, WhatsApp) smaller below a divider; keep 2–3 links visible beside the hamburger ('combo' nav) and repeat key links in the footer.

MOBILE BOTTOM BAR: persistent 4-tab bar (Home, Shop, Bag, WhatsApp) with ≥48px targets, bottom-anchored for thumb reach; on product pages replace it with a sticky bar showing price + 'Add to bag' + WhatsApp icon that slides up only after the primary CTA scrolls out of view; bag drawer auto-opens after add with the item + fabric/colour/pieces, qty, subtotal and a single primary CTA 'Send bag on WhatsApp' (wa.me link with pre-filled multi-line message) plus 'View full bag' escape hatch; respect `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`.

PERFORMANCE GUARDRAILS: poster is the LCP — keep it ≤80 KB AVIF/WebP with fetchpriority=high; everything else lazy; no scroll-linked effects on mobile except reveals; transforms/opacity only; `will-change` sparingly; Safari caps Lenis at 60/30 fps so test on a real iPhone in Low Power Mode and with Chrome 'Data Saver'; budget ≤2 MB hero video, ≤150 KB JS for the motion stack (gsap core + ScrollTrigger + SplitText + lenis ≈ fits), and set a global `prefers-reduced-motion` kill-switch that also stops the marquee and Ken Burns.

REFERENCE BOARD for the designer: Toteme (image-tile home, grid/lifestyle toggle, WhatsApp in footer), The Row (nav + archive depth, serif wordmark black on cream), Jacquemus (single-typeface, hairline-rule system), Bottega Veneta (muted video hero + custom serif), Sézane and Marine Serre (Siteinspire 2026), Serotoninn / Tilly Sveaas / Deadly Ponies / Coutumes (Awwwards 2026 fashion e-commerce: editorial homepage, product video, variable-type hover, Shopify-grade PLP/PDP).

findings.topic: Fabric vocabulary — women's (names + one-line definitions, paraphrased from Sapphire's Fabric Glossary; counts from Gul Ahmed facets)
findings.detail: Lawn: very light 100% cotton plain weave, summer, soft/absorbent. Slub Lawn: lawn with slub texture. Zari Lawn: lawn with metallic-thread patterns. Textured Lawn (Khaadi facet). Denting Lawn (Gul Ahmed dupatta facet, 12). Cambric: tightly woven smooth fine-finish 100% cotton, summer + mid-season (Gul Ahmed: the default TROUSER fabric, 156 of 371 products). Light Cambric (Alkaram). Khaddar: cotton-yarn fabric, textured, breathable, winter (Gul Ahmed shirt 87 / trouser 94 / dupatta 73). Light Khaddar: lighter khaddar for warmer days (Khaadi, Sapphire). Premium Khaddar / Zari Khaddar / Linen Khaddar (variants). Karandi: textured, breathable, lightweight, mid-season and winter (Gul Ahmed 23 shirt / 23 dupatta / 20 trouser). Linen: durable breathable (Gul Ahmed 16). Cotton Linen. Viscose: soft silky lightweight, good drape; Viscose Slub; Cotton Viscose (Sapphire 'Printed Cotton Viscose Suit'). Jacquard: woven pattern — Self Jacquard (100% cotton, pattern from weave), Yarn Dyed Jacquard, Extra Weft Jacquard (embossed), Broche Jacquard, Kota Jacquard. Dobby: small geometric woven patterns; Cotton Dobby; Mesuri/Messuri Dobby (Khaadi). Fine Cotton Satin. Paper Cotton (Gul Ahmed festive). Corduroy (Gul Ahmed winter 6). Pashmina (winter shawl/dupatta, 9–14). Raw Silk / Viscose Raw Silk / Premium Raw Silk (formal). Velvet (formal). Dupatta-only fabrics: Chiffon (Viscose Chiffon, Blended Chiffon, Bemberg Crinkle Chiffon), Organza (Blended Organza, Zari Line Organza), Net (Khaddi Net, Blended Net, Silk Cotton Net, Cotton Net), Tissue (Blended Tissue, Bemberg Tissue), Voile (Fine Voile, Textured Voile), Shawl (Blended/Viscose/Acrylic/Wool Shawl), Manaar, Multi Neps, Mehsuri. Zellbury adds: Shamoz Silk, Ayuthia, Zari Textured, Yarn Dyed; print style 'Chunri'; embroidery style 'Chikankari'. Gul Ahmed separates fabric per piece into three facets: 'Shirt Fabric' (20 values), 'Dupatta Fabric' (23 values), 'Trouser Fabric' (13 values). findings.topic: Piece counts and configurations (what each piece is)
findings.detail: Standard taxonomy: 1 Piece / 2 Piece / 3 Piece (Khaadi facet 'Category: 1, 2, 3 Piece' and 'Size: 1PC/2PC/3PC'; Gul Ahmed 'Piece: 1 Piece (10), 2 Piece (41), 3 Piece (320)'; Sapphire nav 'Shop by Piece: 1/2/3 Piece' plus 'Unstitched Bottoms'). 3 Piece = Shirt (kameez/top) + Trouser (shalwar/bottom) + Dupatta (or Shawl in winter — Sapphire lists 'Shawl' as the third piece on khaddar suits). 2 Piece is AMBIGUOUS and must be spelled out: either Shirt + Trouser (Alkaram 'RTS | Shirt & Trouser'; Gul Ahmed '2 Piece Printed Lawn Suit with Printed Trouser'; Khaadi URL 'fabrics-2-piece-top-and-bottom') or Shirt + Dupatta (Zellbury 'Shirt Dupatta - 1064'; Gul Ahmed eBay listing 'Khaddar Shirt/Dupatta'). 1 Piece = shirt fabric only (Gul Ahmed 'One Piece Collection'). Zellbury encodes this as a facet named 'Specs' with values 'Shirt Shalwar Dupatta' | 'Shirt Shalwar' | 'Shirt Dupatta', and sells singles under 'Unstitched Trouser' and 'Dupatta'. Naming of the bottom varies: 'Trouser' (Gul Ahmed, Sapphire, Alkaram, Bonanza, Sana Safinaz), 'Bottom' (Khaadi), 'Shalwar' (Zellbury), 'Pants' (Sana Safinaz older). Naming of top: 'Shirt' (most), 'Top' (Khaadi). Men's = one single fabric length for the whole kameez shalwar ('Unstitched Suit', '2 Piece' in Sapphire men's facet), not a multi-piece kit.

findings.topic: Meters — men's shalwar kameez fabric
findings.detail: Brand standard is a single 4.5 m length: J. 'Length: 4.5 meters' (all 150 products), Edenrobe 'Length: 4.5 meters, Width: approx 1.10–1.15 meters', Gul Ahmed '4.5 MTR Suit Width 36 in', Cambridge 'Cutting: 4.5m' (with '4.25 Meter Fabric' on the same listing), Bonanza snippet 'Length: 4.5 M, Width: 56"'. findings.topic: Care instructions — copy patterns actually published
findings.detail: KHAADI (cloth-care page): 'Machine wash cold, gentle or delicate' / 'Do not bleach' / 'Line dry in shade' / 'Warm iron if needed; do not iron embellishment' + 'follow the care label'. ALKARAM (PDP, bold 'Care Instructions:'): 'Dry clean only. Do not use bleach. Can be ironed.' EDENROBE (men, 'Fabric Care' tab): Washing — machine wash cold with like colours, gentle cycle, mild detergent; Bleaching — do not bleach or use harsh chemicals; Drying — tumble dry low or hang dry, avoid high heat; Ironing — low heat, avoid direct contact with prints/embellishments; Dry cleaning — follow dry cleaner's instructions if labelled; Storage — cool dry place, avoid prolonged direct sunlight. ZELLBURY (budget cotton): 'All fabric is pre-shrunk', 'Cotton is machine washable; warm water recommended', 'Hang dry; high dryer setting can be used', 'Iron on a high temperature', 'Avoid over-bleaching (damage/yellowing)'. NARKIN'S (men's fabric brand, dedicated 'Fabric & Clothing Care Guide'): Unstitched — first wash hand wash separately in cold water; mild detergent, no strong powders/bleach; soak max 5–10 min; avoid hot water (colour + shrinkage); do not wring/twist, squeeze and hang in shade; iron medium heat on reverse, thin cloth over soft cotton/blends; store cool dry, fold in fabric bag; 'Pre-wash cotton before stitching to reduce shrinkage'; 'premium suiting and wash & wear should be dry cleaned for the first wash'; avoid fabric softener on wash & wear. ZARA SHAHJAHAN UK (tailoring guide): natural cottons (lawn, cambric, linen) shrink — 'soak the shirt and trouser fabric in cold water for 15-20 minutes each, then dry flat in the shade' before cutting. COCO by Zara Shahjahan (luxury): 'Iron at moderate temperature. Do not use any bleach or stain removing chemical. Dry Clean only. Do not expose fabric to direct sunlight.' Gul Ahmed, Sapphire, J., Sana Safinaz, Bonanza: no care text on the PDP (Gul Ahmed has a 'Fabric & care' tab that only lists fabric per piece). INFERRED split for a shop: lawn/cotton/cambric/khaddar = cold hand/machine wash, shade dry, no bleach, pre-wash before stitching; wash & wear / blended = machine wash cold or dry-clean first wash, low iron; embroidered/sequin/organza = dry clean only, never iron embellishment.

findings.topic: Size guidance for unstitched — none; what brands publish instead (tailoring/measurement)
findings.detail: No brand offers sizes on unstitched: Khaadi's 'Size' is just 1PC/2PC/3PC; J.'s 'Size' is '4.5 Meters'. No Pakistani brand PDP ties a stitching service to the unstitched product (Khaadi's 'Tailored' is an RTW line; J./Bonanza/Gul Ahmed searches found no stitching form). The only Pakistani-brand measurement copy found is NISHAT LINEN's Size Guide (used for RTW but written as a how-to-measure): fields and instructions — Shoulder (across back, bone to bone); Bust (under arms at fullest part, tape level with shoulder blades); Waist (narrowest point, above navel below rib cage); Hips (widest part, ~20 cm below waist); Neck width (centre front to desired width); Sleeve length (shoulder tip toward wrist); Sleeve opening (across wrist at sleeve bottom); Length (top of shoulder to required length); Ankle length (barefoot, shoulder to ankle); Floor level (barefoot, shoulder to floor = full length without heels); Trouser waist (waistband sits ~2 inches below navel); units 'All measurements in inches (1 inch = 2.5cm)'; general 'Stand upright and look straight ahead'; men's chart snippet: shoulder 16.5–20 in, trouser waist 26.5–37 in, shalwar length 37–40 in (XS–XL). General salwar-kameez guides (Indian: Utsav, Lashkaraa, Aza) add: Chest/Bust, Shoulder, Sleeve length, Kameez length (top of shoulder over bust to hem), Shalwar/trouser length (waist to ankle), Hips, Armhole, Upper arm, Neck depth front/back; tips — measure over thin clothing, don't hold breath, get help for back/length, keep the numbers for future orders. Zara Shahjahan guide: give tailor the campaign photo for border/lace placement, specify lining (fine lawn/chiffon needs a 'shameez'), state shirt length, sleeve style, trouser style (straight / culottes / shalwar). Alkaram men's guide: 'confirm requirements with your tailor before cutting'. findings.topic: Delivery, COD and exchange norms in Pakistan (brand policies as published)
findings.detail: GUL AHMED: PDP block 'Estimated Delivery — Karachi/Lahore: 24 to 48 hrs; Major cities (Islamabad, Multan, Faisalabad, Quetta...): 3 to 4 working days; Rest of Pakistan: 4 to 5 working days'; flat PKR 249 shipping; COD after telephonic verification; 30-day 'no-questions-asked' exchange but must notify within 3 days of delivery via complaint form; free pickup, 7–10 working days; unused, unwashed, tags + invoice; no cash refunds; fragrance/jewellery excluded; 'excess fabric used during shoots is not provided'. SAPPHIRE: 5–7 working days (up to 15 in sales); PKR 249 under Rs 8,000, free above Rs 8,000 (non-sale); COD cash only, large orders verified; 30-day exchange (online or in-store), sale items + fragrances excluded; returns only for wrong/defective; refunds as credit voucher only; Leopards Courier drop-off. ALKARAM: Karachi 2–3 / rest 3–5 working days (5–7 in sales); flat PKR 250; COD must be verified via a link sent to the customer's WhatsApp; 'pay the rider before opening the package'; 7-day exchange, defective/wrong only, photo evidence; sale items no return; no cash refund, voucher valid 1 month; customer pays return shipping if they 'simply dislike' it. J.: 1–3 working days major cities, 3–5 elsewhere (longer in sales); return/exchange within 3 days only if damaged/defective/incorrect/incomplete, unused with tags. EDENROBE: Karachi 1–2 / outside 4–5 working days (5–7 in grand sales); PKR 200 prepaid / PKR 250 COD; COD only under PKR 40,000 (partial advance above); 14-day exchange, faulty or original condition with tags + receipt; items at 50%+ off, fragrances, accessories excluded; missing-item claims need an unboxing video within 2 days; exchange via phone, WhatsApp +92 301 6747453, email, or online form. KHAADI (search snippets of khaadi.com policy pages; direct fetch 404): COD nationwide under PKR 50,000 (Rs 49,999 cap); courier collects before parcel opened; order confirmed by OTP via SMS/email; delivery fee from Rs 120; Karachi/Lahore/Islamabad 2–4 days, other cities 7–10; max 2 orders per 24 h; two delivery attempts; 7-day exchange at any store, unused with tags + invoice, sale items excluded; defects reported within 3 days with photos; voucher not cash. SANA SAFINAZ: flat PKR 250; 'never asks customers to make online payments for COD orders' scam warning. BONANZA: 2–3 working days nationwide; 14-day exchange; 'No Return or Exchange on Sale Items'. ZELLBURY: 'Buy 3 items & Get Free Delivery', free delivery on online payments, 30-day exchange/return with invoice + tags, discounted items excluded. NARKIN'S: free shipping over Rs 10,000 via TCS. HOUSE OF ITTEHAD: flat PKR 99, 3–5 working days, 10-day exchange, PKR 250 fee for preference exchanges. MARKAZ marketplace: COD in Karachi/Lahore/Faisalabad/Islamabad/Rawalpindi/Peshawar, dispatch 24–48 h, 3–5 business days, 7-day return. No brand carves out unstitched fabric from its exchange policy; all require 'unused/uncut, tags intact'. Couriers named: Leopards, TCS, DHL (intl).

findings.topic: How WhatsApp ordering is presented on Pakistani sites
findings.detail: Big brands use WhatsApp for SUPPORT and SHARING, not ordering: 'Share this Look → WhatsApp' (Sapphire), 'Share on WhatsApp' (J.), WhatsApp share icon (Edenrobe), 'WhatsApp contact link + WhatsApp Channel link + Track Your Order' in header (Edenrobe), 'UAN/WhatsApp: 021-111-003-005' (Sana Safinaz), exchange requests via WhatsApp number (Edenrobe), COD order verification 'through a link sent to the customer's WhatsApp number' (Alkaram), floating WhatsApp chat link (Bonanza). WhatsApp-ONLY fabric shops (reachable, fetched): ROYAL CITY FABRICS (Abbottabad) — number repeated in top bar, nav, hero, every product card, contact, FAQ, terms, footer and a floating 'Chat with us!' button; CTA labels verbatim: 'Order on WhatsApp' (hero), 'Inquire Now' (each product card), 'View All Collections on WhatsApp', 'Chat on WhatsApp', 'Order Now on WhatsApp' (closing CTA); each button opens wa.me with a pre-filled greeting naming the collection; copy: 'Free delivery on orders above PKR 5,000', 'Cash on Delivery (COD) available across Pakistan', payment 'COD, bank transfer, JazzCash/EasyPaisa', 'team responds instantly', 'free fabric-selection consultation on WhatsApp', 'WhatsApp updates throughout delivery', 'Express delivery available for urgent orders'; trust badges '100% Original', 'Branded Fabrics', '4.8 rating', '150+ Reviews', '1,600+ happy customers', 'Since 2020'; product cards have NO price/meters/colour (only title, blurb, 3 bullets, Inquire Now). DADA FABRICS (Lahore) 'WhatsApp Order' page — headings 'Order on WhatsApp', 'Place Your Order Now', 'WhatsApp Now', 'Available Categories', 'Delivery Information', 'Why Choose Us?'; 4-step how-to: (1) send a screenshot or the product name, (2) share quantity and details, (3) give name, delivery address, contact number, (4) team confirms the order; buttons 'Order Now on WhatsApp', 'Chat With Us', 'Buy via WhatsApp', 'Quick Order', 'Send Inquiry'; wa.me link pre-filled 'Assalamualaikum I want to place an order'; copy 'Cash on Delivery Available', 'Pakistan bhar mein secure aur fast delivery available', 'Lahore se nationwide shipping' (Roman-Urdu mixed); badges 'Premium Quality Products', 'Fast Shipping Across Pakistan', 'Wholesale & Retail Orders Accepted', 'Customer Satisfaction Guaranteed'. Observed weaknesses to avoid: inconsistent delivery copy ('3-5 business days' vs '2-5 days'), unanswered FAQ 'How can I place an order?', placeholder number on template demos.

findings.topic: Reachability log
findings.detail: Fetched directly (reachable=true): Khaadi (home, /fabrics/, PDP, cloth-care, customer-service; policy pages 404 — policy data from search snippets of khaadi.com), Sapphire (home, 3-piece listing, men's listing, PDP incl. offset read, women's + men's fabric glossaries, FAQs, exchanges-return), Gul Ahmed (home, unstitched listing + facets, 3 PDPs, men's listing, men's PDP, shipping policy, refund policy), Alkaram (home, RTS listing, PDP, shipment, refund policy), J. (home, men's unstitched listing, PDP), Edenrobe (home, men's listing, PDP, shipping, return policy), Sana Safinaz (home, unstitched listing, PDP via search-found slug), Bonanza Satrangi (3pc listing, PDP), Zellbury (listing, PDP), Nishat Linen (size guides), Narkin's (care guide, buyer guide), Royal City Fabrics, DADA Fabrics, Zara Shahjahan UK guide, Alkaram men's blog. reachable=false / partial: Cambridge (cambridgeshop.com is a parked GoDaddy domain; cambridge.com.pk 301→thecambridgeshop.com whose pages fetch as title-only, JS-rendered; product data from search snippets of thecambridgeshop.com), Khaadi policy pages (404s; snippets used), Sapphire shipping-policy and fabric-glossary index pages (content behind JS), 'Dynamic Store' WhatsApp demo (products not rendered). Items labelled INFERRED above were not seen on a brand page.

recommendations: Product data model (field names drawn from the brands): sku (design code, e.g. 'BC-L26-014'), title (pattern '3 Piece Printed Lawn Suit with Printed Lawn Dupatta' or '3 Piece - Embroidered Lawn Suit'), subtitle ('Printed | Lawn'), gender ('women'|'men'), pieces (1|2|3), pieceConfig ('shirt-trouser-dupatta'|'shirt-trouser'|'shirt-dupatta'|'shirt'|'single-length'), components[] each {piece: 'shirt'|'trouser'|'dupatta'|'shawl', fabric: 'Lawn'|'Cambric'|'Khaddar'|'Karandi'|'Linen'|'Wash & Wear'|'Cotton'|'Viscose'|'Chiffon'..., treatment: 'Printed'|'Digital Printed'|'Paste Printed'|'Dyed'|'Yarn Dyed'|'Embroidered'|'Printed Embroidered', meters: 2.5, parts?: [{name:'front'|'back'|'sleeves'|'border'|'neckline', treatment, meters|pieces}], colourName}, fabricFamily (facet value), dupattaFabric (separate facet like Gul Ahmed/Sapphire), trouserFabric, type ('Printed'|'Embroidered'), colourFamily (13-value facet), colourName (named shade: 'Tea Pink', 'Bottle Green'), swatches[] (men: one article, 3–6 colours), season ('Summer'|'Pre-Fall'|'Winter'|'Festive'|'All Seasons'), collection ('Lawn 2026 Vol 2', 'Winter Khaddar '26', 'Eid Edit'), tier ('Essential'|'Signature'|'Luxury'), lengthMeters + widthInches (men only: 4.5 m, 36"/56"), addOns ['Brand label','Matching buttons'] (men), price, compareAtPrice, discountPct, availability, careInstructions[], disclaimer, estimatedDelivery per city tier, tags.

'What's in the box' block: use a per-piece card list titled 'Component Details' / 'What's in the suit' with one line per piece in the brand grammar '<Treatment> <Fabric> <Piece> — <N> m' (e.g. 'Printed Lawn Shirt — 3.0 m', 'Dyed Cambric Trouser — 2.5 m', 'Printed Lawn Dupatta — 2.5 m'; embroidered: 'Embroidered Lawn Front — 1.15 m', 'Printed Lawn Back & Sleeves — 1.85 m', 'Embroidered Sleeve Border — 1 piece'); show a total-meters chip; for men a single line 'Fabric length: 4.5 m · Width: 36 in · Enough for one kameez shalwar' plus 'Includes brand label & matching buttons'. Always state the bottom as 'Trouser / Shalwar' and label 2-piece as 'Shirt + Trouser' or 'Shirt + Dupatta' explicitly.

Default meter values if the shop has not measured a product: women shirt 3.0 m, trouser/shalwar 2.5 m, dupatta 2.5 m (lawn dupatta) or 2.25 m (chiffon) — marked 'approx.'; men 4.5 m (budget lines 4 m); add Sana Safinaz-style note 'Minor variations in measurements may occur' and a shrinkage note for pure cottons.

Care block (copy-ready, split by fabric family): Lawn/Cotton/Cambric/Khaddar — 'Pre-wash in cold water before stitching (lawn and cambric can shrink)', 'Hand or machine wash cold, gentle cycle, mild detergent', 'Do not bleach', 'Line dry in shade — direct sun fades dye', 'Warm iron on reverse; do not iron over embroidery'. Wash & Wear / Blended (men) — 'Machine wash cold with like colours, gentle', 'Dry clean recommended for first wash', 'Hang dry, no high heat', 'Low iron', 'No fabric softener'. Embroidered / Organza / Sequins — 'Dry clean only', 'Do not iron embellishment', 'Store folded away from humidity'. Use Khaadi-style icon row (wash / bleach / dry / iron / dry-clean) linking to a fabric-care guide page that doubles as the Fabric Glossary.

Disclaimer copy (every brand has one; reuse verbatim style): 'Actual product colour and texture may vary slightly from the image due to photographic lighting and screen settings.' plus 'Only items listed under Component Details are included; extra fabric or embellishments shown in styling photos are not supplied.'

Size & measurement guide page (instead of a size selector): title 'Unstitched — one size, your tailor's fit'; fields in inches with how-to lines copied from Nishat's structure: Shoulder, Chest/Bust, Waist, Hips, Neck width/depth, Sleeve length, Sleeve opening (cuff), Kameez length, Shalwar/Trouser length, Trouser waist (sits ~2 in below navel), Ankle vs floor length note; tips: measure over thin clothing, stand upright, get help for back/length, save your numbers; a 'Tell your tailor' checklist (shirt length, sleeve style, neckline, trouser style straight/culotte/shalwar, lining/shameez for sheer lawn, border placement — show them the product photo); local stitching cost benchmark 'Rs 900–1,700 per suit in most Faisalabad tailors' marked as indicative; include a downloadable/shareable measurement card the customer can send on WhatsApp.

Filters to implement (matching the leaders): Gender, Pieces (1/2/3) + Piece config, Fabric (shirt), Dupatta fabric, Trouser fabric, Type (Printed/Embroidered), Colour family (13 values + swatches), Price bands 'Under Rs 3,000 / 3,000–6,000 / 6,000–10,000 / 10,000+', Season, Collection, Discount band, Availability; sort by Featured / Newest / Price asc-desc / Best selling.

Price presentation: 'Rs. 4,290' format with strikethrough compareAt and a '-24%' badge; keep Baig Cloth bands realistic for Faisalabad: women printed lawn/cotton 3pc Rs 2,500–4,500, embroidered 3pc Rs 4,500–8,000, 2pc Rs 1,800–3,500, winter khaddar/karandi 3pc Rs 3,500–6,500; men wash & wear 4–4.5 m Rs 2,000–4,500, cotton/latha Rs 2,500–5,000, karandi Rs 3,000–6,000, boski/premium Rs 6,000–10,000 (bands INFERRED from observed brand and marketplace prices).
